sets.title: Process vs Result
sets.description: Choose the right aspect based on what is being emphasized
sets.descriptionRussian: Выберите вид глагола в зависимости от акцента

items.prompt: Что ты делал вчера вечером? - Я _____ книгу. (What were you doing? - I was reading.)
items.promptEnglish: What were you doing last night? - I was reading a book.
items.hint: The question asks about the activity/process, not the result.
items.explanation: When someone asks 'What were you doing?' they ask about the activity, so imperfective: читал.

items.prompt: Ты _____ мою книгу? Я хочу её забрать. (Have you finished my book? I want to take it back.)
items.promptEnglish: Have you finished reading my book? I want to take it back.
items.hint: The speaker wants to know about the result: is the book finished?
items.explanation: The focus is on the result (is it done?), so perfective: прочитал.

items.prompt: Ты когда-нибудь _____ Достоевского? (Have you ever read Dostoevsky?)
items.hint: Asking about general life experience, not a specific completed book.
items.explanation: General experience questions ('have you ever...?') use imperfective: читал.

items.prompt: Наконец я _____ эту задачу! (I finally solved this problem!)
Я не _____ эту книгу. (I haven't read this book. - general denial)
items.promptEnglish: I haven't read this book (general statement).
items.hint: General negation (I have no experience of reading it) prefers imperfective.
items.explanation: General denial of experience uses imperfective: не читал = 'I haven't read it (at all).'

items.prompt: Я уже _____ завтрак, спасибо. (I've already eaten breakfast, thanks.)
items.explanation: Уже + result = perfective: позавтракал. The breakfast is done.

items.prompt: Кто _____ окно? Здесь холодно! (Who opened the window? It's cold!)
items.promptEnglish: Who opened the window? It's cold here!
items.hint: The speaker sees a result (cold air) and asks who caused it.
items.explanation: Asking about who caused a visible result uses perfective: кто открыл?

minimalPairs.context: Ты _____ этот фильм? (Have you ever seen this movie? - general experience)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Have you ever seen this movie?
minimalPairs.explanation: General experience question uses imperfective: Ты смотрел? = 'Have you ever seen?'

minimalPairs.context: Ты _____ этот фильм? Расскажи, чем закончился! (Did you watch/finish this movie? Tell me how it ended!)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Did you finish watching this movie? Tell me the ending!
minimalPairs.explanation: Asking about completion (to discuss the ending) uses perfective: посмотрел.

minimalPairs.context: Кто _____ суп? Тут кастрюля на плите. (Who was cooking soup? There's a pot on the stove.)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Who was cooking soup? (There's a pot on the stove.)
minimalPairs.explanation: Asking about the activity/process (who was doing it?) uses imperfective: варил.

minimalPairs.context: Кто _____ суп? Он очень вкусный! (Who made this soup? It's delicious!)
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Who made this soup? It's delicious!
minimalPairs.explanation: Asking about who produced the result (delicious soup) uses perfective: сварил.

sets.title: Fill and Correct
sets.description: Fill in the correct aspect and fix mistakes
sets.descriptionRussian: Заполните правильный вид и исправьте ошибки

blanks: Ты когда-нибудь _____ в Японии? (Have you ever been to Japan? - general experience)
Я уже _____ домашнее задание. (I've already done my homework. - result)
Весь день мы _____ квартиру. (We were cleaning the apartment all day. - process)
Кто _____ мою чашку? Она разбита! (Who broke my cup? It's broken! - result)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Experience = imperfective; result = perfective; process/duration = imperfective
hints: General life experience (когда-нибудь) uses which aspect?
Duration (весь день) emphasizes the process. Which aspect?
Visible result (broken cup) and asking who caused it. Which aspect?
explanations: General experience uses imperfective: был (been). Ты был в Японии?
Asking about who caused a result uses perfective: разбил.

errorCorrection.explanation: General experience questions use imperfective: читал Толстого? (Have you ever read Tolstoy?)

errorCorrection.hint: Долго emphasizes the duration of the process, not the result.
errorCorrection.explanation: Duration (долго) requires imperfective: решал (worked on it for a long time), not perfective решил.

errorCorrection.sentence: Он не писал мне ответ. Я всё ещё жду.
errorCorrection.hint: The speaker is waiting for a result (the reply). The negation is about a missing result.
errorCorrection.explanation: Negation of an expected result uses perfective: не написал (hasn't written/produced the reply).

items.prompt: Which aspect is used for general denial of experience?
items.promptEnglish: I didn't read / haven't read / never read this book.
items.hint: Не читал = I haven't read (general). Не прочитал = I didn't finish reading (specific).
items.explanation: General negation of experience uses imperfective: не читал (I haven't read it). Perfective не прочитал means 'I didn't finish it.'

items.prompt: Вчера весь вечер мы _____ старые фотографии. (All evening we were looking at old photos.)
items.promptEnglish: All evening we were looking at old photos.
items.explanation: Duration (весь вечер) emphasizes the process: смотрели (imperfective).

items.prompt: Вы _____ эту задачу? Покажите мне ответ. (Have you solved this problem? Show me the answer.)
items.promptEnglish: Have you solved this problem? Show me the answer.
items.hint: The speaker wants to see the result (the answer).
items.explanation: Asking about a result (show me the answer) uses perfective: решили.

sets.title: Patterns and Sort
sets.description: Recognize aspect patterns and sort by emphasis
sets.descriptionRussian: Распознайте паттерны и рассортируйте по акценту

patternRecognition.sentence: Ты читал эту книгу? / Ты был в Париже? / Ты пробовал суши?
patternRecognition.question: What type of question is this, and why is imperfective used?
patternRecognition.explanation: These ask about life experience, not specific results. Imperfective shows the focus is on whether the experience happened, not on completion.

patternRecognition.sentence: Кто открыл окно? Кто разбил чашку? Кто написал это письмо?
patternRecognition.question: Why is perfective used in all these questions?
options: The speaker asks about who caused a visible result
The speaker asks about habitual actions
The speaker asks about a process
patternRecognition.answer: The speaker asks about who caused a visible result
patternRecognition.explanation: Each question points to a visible result (open window, broken cup, written letter) and asks who produced it. Result focus = perfective.

patternRecognition.sentence: Я не читал / Я не смотрел / Я не слышал
patternRecognition.question: What does imperfective negation express?
options: General denial: 'I haven't done it at all'
patternRecognition.answer: General denial: 'I haven't done it at all'
patternRecognition.explanation: Imperfective negation = general denial of experience. Не читал = 'I haven't read it.' Perfective не прочитал would mean 'I didn't finish reading.'

categorySorting.instruction: Sort: Is the speaker focusing on PROCESS or RESULT?

items.word: Что ты делал вчера? - Я читал.

blanks: Что вы _____ на уроке? (What did you do in class? - asking about activity)
Кто _____ эту картину? Она прекрасна! (Who painted this picture? It's beautiful! - result)
Я никогда не _____ на лошади. (I've never ridden a horse. - general experience)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Activity = imperfective; result = perfective; experience = imperfective
hints: Asking about what activity was done (process focus).
Admiring a result and asking who produced it.
explanations: Asking about activity/process uses imperfective: делали.
Asking about who produced a result uses perfective: нарисовал.
General experience (никогда не) uses imperfective: ездил.

sets.title: Mixed Challenge
sets.description: Advanced aspect choices in various contexts
sets.descriptionRussian: Сложные аспектные выборы в разных контекстах

items.prompt: Ты _____ ей о встрече? (Did you tell her about the meeting? - did the information reach her?)
items.promptEnglish: Did you tell her about the meeting? (Did the message get across?)
items.hint: The question is about whether the result was achieved (she was informed).
items.explanation: Focus on the result (information delivered): perfective сказал.

items.prompt: О чём вы _____? (What were you talking about? - activity)
items.hint: Asking about the content of the conversation (activity/process).
items.explanation: Asking about the activity of talking uses imperfective: говорили.

items.prompt: Она _____ нам торт. Вот он, на столе. (She baked us a cake. Here it is, on the table.)
items.promptEnglish: She baked us a cake. Here it is, on the table.
items.hint: The cake exists as a result (it's on the table).
items.explanation: Visible result (cake on the table) uses perfective: испекла.

errorCorrection.explanation: Experience question: когда-нибудь + imperfective: решал (Have you ever done a crossword?).

errorCorrection.sentence: Кто открывал мою сумку? Вещи разбросаны!
errorCorrection.hint: The speaker sees a result (things scattered) and asks who caused it.
errorCorrection.explanation: Visible result focus requires perfective: кто открыл? (Who opened it, producing this mess?)

errorCorrection.hint: Долго emphasizes duration/process, which needs imperfective.
errorCorrection.explanation: Duration (долго) requires imperfective: строила (built for a long time), not perfective построила.

translation.english: Have you ever been to Moscow?
translation.hint: General experience = imperfective: был. в Москве = in Moscow (prepositional)

translation.english: Who broke the vase? It's on the floor!
translation.answer: Кто разбил вазу? Она на полу!
translation.hint: Asking about who caused a visible result = perfective: разбил
